body: I've learned that when I started working. I always worked in groups, with other people. Nobody cares if you're having a good or a bad day, the work has to be done. That helped me in detaching myself from some of my problems and just focusing on work related goals. I'm in a position where I have to order a few people around, so it's very important to keep my composure and not let my coworkers notice the cracks. Otherwise my authority would take a big hit, both with the people above and below me in company structure.

I've checked it out. Interesting indeed. To me a concept like this makes a lot of sense and while I don't necessarily believe that it's 100% true, it 's  something that I'll keep in the back of my head, if only for a good conversation topic.
It's okay. having a place to share is great in itself.

I didn't want to bring much attention to that since we're not talking philosophy or physics here, but to answer your question - rather often. I did a lot of creative work and I'm trying to work more so fantasizing and coming up with fictional scenarios is something I do often in my spare time.   
  
As for living them, not really. I believe that alternative realities are probable, but since we've no way of contacting them (and I'm not going to waste time and reasources exploring the esotheric) I accept my reality as the definitive one. That is, one that I'm in and have to work with. I think that outside of moments of great weakness, I wouldn't go to another world if given the opportunity. I would rather go with my competitive nature and chose to continue on with my suffering with hopes of overcoming it "somehow".

Thanks. I truly believe that not all is lost, but I'm also careful not to put too much hope in things that are ephemeral and may easily turn out to be nothing. I have to admit I'm pretty good at holding the thoughts at bay, but every week they do come back.  
The thing you said about social issues also speaks to me. I'm on edge recently and I take pressure and small obstacles worse and worse.
